heading: Your self-issued IDs
sub: A wallet can sign you in with an ID Token it signs with its own key (Self-Issued OpenID Provider v2). Nobody vouches for that key, so it signs in only the person who enrolled it here.
subject: Subject
label: Label
locationAppTip: Name reported by the wallet app: {name}
locationAppUnnamedTip: A wallet app answered the request; it did not name itself.
locationDcApiTip: Answered through your browser's Digital Credentials API.
locationDcApiOriginTip: Answered through your browser's Digital Credentials API, on {origin}.
locationAdminTip: Added by an administrator; no wallet was involved.
locationNoneTip: Enrolled before this service recorded where a key came from. Proving it again with your wallet records it.
preferredNoteOn: Your preferred DID is one you proved with your wallet. An application you allow to see it — on the consent screen, for the did scope — is told it as the did claim. It is the same value everywhere, so applications that are told it could recognise you as one person. Only a DID you proved can be preferred.
preferredNoteOff: Your preferred DID is one you proved with your wallet. This service does not release it to applications here at present; the mark is kept for when it does.
donePreferred: That DID is now your preferred one.
doneUnpreferred: You have no preferred DID now; none is released.
enrolNote: Your wallet is asked for a self-issued ID Token, and the key that signed it is enrolled for you — you prove you hold it; nothing is typed.
reprove: Enrolling a key that is already here proves it again: do that if your wallet's did:web key changed, and an administrator's entry becomes one you proved.
off: Signing in with a self-issued ID is turned off here, so no wallet can be enrolled from this page. The keys above stay enrolled.
doneEnrolled: Your wallet's key is enrolled. It signs you in from now on.
doneRemoved: That key no longer signs you in.
